Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. _Reviewed September 5, 2026, 1:52 PM ET / 17:52 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes Adds a session-menu action that copies public preview links, generic social-card pages and build-generated artwork, with deployment guidance for login proxies. ## Merge readiness ✅ **Ready for maintainer review** Keep open: this adds a distinct capability absent from inspected main. No blocking correctness findings were identified, and the maintainer label independently excludes automated closure. **Priority:** P3 **Reviewed head:** `8f4a434014e56c5ee06e875b6343c4fda2cf766c` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A focused implementation with useful boundary coverage and no identified blocking defect; runtime results are contributor-reported. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: The maintainer-author exemption applies. The captured body reports browser copy/open behavior and HTTP isolation checks; linked images were inaccessible here, and no screenshot-based security claim is accepted. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: The maintainer-author exemption applies. The captured body reports browser copy/open behavior and HTTP isolation checks; linked images were inaccessible here, and no screenshot-based security claim is accepted. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 11 items | Verified review scope: Origin identifies openclaw/openclaw. Raw test-merge parents match the pinned main followed by the exact PR head; its main-relative changes match the introduced files. Unrelated model-selection and outbound-delivery changes are base drift.
Public document boundary: The preview owner parses the existing session URL grammar, preserves encoded paths, retains only catalog routing parameters, escapes interpolated values, and performs no session lookup. Its response disables scripts and uses no-store and no-referrer policies.
HTTP routing and sibling isolation: The standalone handler terminates share requests before ordinary plugin dispatch, including when the UI is disabled. The card maps to one static file through existing containment checks; bootstrap authorization remains separate. Approval, focus, media, and plugin routing were inspected. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Control UI turns session-menu selections into Gateway URLs. The Gateway serves generic preview metadata and artwork, then directs visitors to the existing authenticated session view. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Session menu] --> B[Build preview URL] B --> C[Gateway preview route] D[Link crawler or visitor] --> C C --> E[Generic page and static card] E --> F[Open session link] F --> G[Existing authentication] G --> H[Session or dashboard] ``` ## Before merge None.

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Not applicable: this adds a preview capability; it does not report a broken existing contract. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes: a separate state-free document addresses crawler access without exposing authenticated session content; adding metadata only inside the app would leave the login-proxy problem unresolved. Shiny media proof means a screenshot, video, or linked artifact directly shows the changed behavior. Runtime, network, CSP, and security claims still need visible diagnostics. ### Workflow - ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR. - Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments. - A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch. - PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only. - Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only. - Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge. - Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`. - Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation.

Landing checks for [8f4a434014e5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8f4a434014e56c5ee06e875b6343c4fda2cf766c):

- Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The latest ClawSweeper review also has no findings or pre-merge actions.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33981942018) passed on attempt 2, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- The first browser shard run missed an A2UI `board.event` after the light-theme Refresh data click. The same head passed the targeted job rerun. Both unchanged dark→light cases also passed locally with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/board-a2ui.e2e.test.ts`. No timeout or assertion was weakened.
- Prior focused HTTP/navigation proof, the CI-artifact build, changed-file checks, and inspected synthetic copy/open screenshots are recorded in the PR body.

The public boundary remains generic and state-free: it never looks up a session, and its destination retains normal authentication. Production/build +156 lines implement that new capability; tests +146 and docs +42. No new configuration, dependency, or storage contract.

Follow-up if the A2UI event failure recurs: capture its click/bridge lifecycle and inner-widget error before choosing a repair. Its owner files are unchanged by this PR.

Proxy exposure remains an operator deployment step; this merge does not enable the public path on any running instance. Proceeding through native prepare/merge.

Merged via squash.
